newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Market down on crude's decline.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Market down on crude's decline.

text.p: Singapore oil product swaps opened weaker at midday on Wednesday on lower overnight crude values following the release of bearish American Petroleum Statistics (API) figures, market sources said.
"The market is down in line with the crude market but most players are on the sides and trading is thin," one broker said.

January gas oil swaps traded this morning at $30.95, $31.05 and $31.10 a barrel, brokers said. The market eased slightly at midday and was last quoted at $30.90/$31.00, down about 70 cents from Tuesday's values, they said.
The big fall mirrored the hefty 81 cent drop on January Brent crude prices on Tuesday on London's International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) to $23.25 a barrel.
January gas oil futures on the IPE also closed weaker, down $2.00 a tonne to $214.75.

The big fall to crude prices was caused by bearish API figures which showed a climb in crude oil stocks by 324,000 barrels, in distillates stocks by over two million barrels and a build in gasoline of almost six million barrels.
Jet fuel prices also fell in tandem with the gas oil market with the jet fuel/gas oil swaps spread or regrade holding steady.
Brokers said the January regrade was bid at $1.90 a barrel just under the $2.00 traded mark on Tuesday evening.
Fuel oil was steady with support seen from the regional market with range bound trade, brokers said.
January swaps were last quoted at $118.75/$119.50 per tonne.
Naphtha prices were notionally quoted sharply lower in line with the crude market January swaps called at $24.00/$24.50 a barrel compared to Tuesday's offer price of $25.05, one broker said.
